October 2024
Piker's Oct. 29, 2024, episode features the remaining remarks, including the mentions of lynchings.
At the 6:51:51 mark, Piker presses play on a Jubilee debate video showing Black conservative commentator Xaviaer DuRousseau, who says, "We have all of these woke DA's [district attorneys] who are putting forth policies." Piker pauses the video and laughs, then mocks DuRousseau, saying the following (bolding reflects remarks from edited video):
He said, "We need more Klansmen as DAs, OK? Can we go back to a better time when lynchings were happening? This is what I like as a Black man. Also, there's no real racism in America." My man said "woke DAs," dude. What are you saying?
Moments later, at the 6:53:35 mark, Piker reads aloud a chat message that says, "why you always doing too much with black people leave them alone. The rain-soaked Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi turned into a sea of white turbans, music and cheers on Friday (October 30, 2026) evening as thousands of fans braved hours of rain to catch Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh perform in the capital.
The unseasonal showers, which continued through the day and into the evening, did little to dampen the enthusiasm of concertgoers, who began gathering outside the stadium hours before the show. By evening, the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium Metro station was packed, with queues stretching at its exit as fans made their way to Gate No. 14 of the venue. With no general parking available at the stadium, many opted to travel by Metro. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) had also extended services on all lines (except the Airport Express line) upto midnight for the concertgoers.
The excitement was visible as early as 3 p.m., with fans arriving in groups, some dressed in Dosanjh’s popular white and black kurta-pyjama and turban combination. Several women, too, sported white turbans with their outfits.
Students from universities, including Jamia Millia Islamia and Delhi University, along with residents and visitors from other cities, gathered around the box office. Some were still hoping to get their hands on last-minute tickets.
“We could not get the tickets online, but we really wanted to attend the show. So, we came here in the hope that we might get a last minute ticket or from someone who had an extra one,” a student told The Hindu.
Many fans had travelled from different parts of the country and abroad, with some attending their second or even third Dosanjh concert. The audience was diverse, spanning children, young fans and older couples. Among those Dosanjh invited on stage was a CRPF personnel.
Complaint filed seeking curbs on Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi show
Pooja Bajaj, who had travelled from London, said this was her first time watching the singer perform live. “We have come from London to watch Diljit Dosanjh’s concert. This is the first time I am attending it,” she said excitedly.
Satnam Singh had travelled all the way from Toronto, Canada, specifically for the Delhi show. Having previously attended Dosanjh’s concert in Ludhiana in December, he said he was keen to experience the singer’s performance in the capital as well.
“I had attended the concert in Ludhiana earlier in December. I have come from Toronto, especially for this. I enjoyed Diljit’s concert in Toronto as well,” he said.
For Tarasha Kaur, who arrived with her son and other family members, the evening was an opportunity to finally experience the singer’s performance, after following his concerts through videos.
“My son attended Diljit’s show in Canada and he loved it. Since then, we have wanted to attend too. Now, all of us are together for this show. Earlier, we enjoyed the show through videos and today we are going to do it live,” she said.
“Punjabi pride is so central to Diljit’s personality, and seeing him represent that identity on a global stage makes me immensely proud. He has all the qualities you would expect from an international artiste. He is charming in a very Punjabi way, immensely talented, values his roots and his fans, and is not afraid to make a political statement when needed. That combination is what makes him special,” said Kiran Singh, who had come from Chandigarh to attend Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert.
For one teenage fan, the concert was special as it was the first time her parents had relaxed her curfew to let her attend a show.
“My parents know how big a fan I am of Diljit. His posters are everywhere in my room. I have never stepped out after 7 p.m. alone, but today, for this concert, my parents allowed me to go,” she said.
Another fan had travelled from Ludhiana, Dosanjh’s hometown, to watch him perform in the national capital.
Addressing the crowd, Dosanjh referred to the uncertainty surrounding the Delhi leg of his tour and said several attempts had been made to prevent the first show from taking place.
“We wanted to do the first show in Delhi. Many tried to stop this show, but I’m here and the first show has been done. I am in India until December 20 and will do all the other shows also. Try and stop me,” he told the audience.
The Delhi concert marked the opening leg of Dosanjh’s Aura India Tour 2026, with the singer set to perform in several cities across the country. The show had drawn attention in the days leading up to it after the Delhi Police initially withheld permission over “specific threat-related inputs” and security and law-and-order concerns during the festive season, before clearing it following discussions with the organisers.
Fans also praised the arrangements at the venue, particularly the assistance provided by the event staff and the police.
“The management was too good. Everyone attended to us so well, proper guidance was provided to us. Enjoyed a lot, it was awesome,” a fan said.
Another concertgoer, who was attending his third Dosanjh show and second in Delhi, said the experience was even better than his previous visits.
“This was even better than the previous one. The crowd was very good, and the Delhi Police provided a lot of support. I’m also going to Indore and Lucknow to attend the concert,” he said.
As the show drew to a close around 10 p.m., concertgoers streamed out of the stadium and made their way towards the main road, looking for cabs and auto-rickshaws to get home.

Following the Air Force Aerial Display-2026 event in Varanasi on October 25, which was attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi as the chief guest, Union minister Piyush Goyal took to X to laud the crowd that gathered to witness the show.
“This is the picture of a changing India; this is the confidence of a new India,” he said in his post while claiming that 10 lakh people had gathered at the ghats of Varanasi.

#IndianAirForce
— Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) October 25, 2026
The event was held to commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force under the theme “Wings over Ganges”.
Several X users commented under Goyal’s post, claiming that the photographs he posted were old. Several users claimed that the photo is an old image from Kumbh Mela. Several people even posted a screenshot from an AI prompt on Google Lens which stated that the image showed crowds from the Kumbh Mela, to refute Goyal’s claim. Some of these comments are shown in the gallery below:
Is The Image Really Old?
The event was reportedly attended by “lakhs of people from far-flung districts of Purvanchal who had gathered along the banks of the Ganga to watch the historic moment.” Alongside PM Modi, defence minister Rajnath Singh, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and governor Anandi Bhen were also present among other dignitaries.
News agency ANI posted several videos from the event showing massive crowds along the ghat, the size of the crowds match those represented in Goyal’s post.
#WATCH | Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh: Prime Minister Narendra Modi witnesses the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi. The programme will commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force and will be held under the theme “Wings over Ganges”.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel, and Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath also present.
(Source: DD News)
— ANI (@ANI) October 25, 2026
The picture posted by Goyal was also used by several other politicians, including Rajya Sabha MPs Satnam Singh Sandhu and Sujeet Kumar. They also posted images of the same crowd from different angles.
Further, we found a vlog on YouTube uploaded by someone who was passing along the ghat on a train prior to the roadshow. The visuals of the ghat posted by him match the images posted by the ministers.
Below is a comparison of a keyframe from the YouTube video with the image posted by Goyal. The size of the crowd, as well as the location, is the same as that shown in Goyal’s post.
Conclusively, the image posted by union minister Piyush Goyal showing a massive crowd is indeed from the Air Force Aerial Display 2026 held on October 25 in Varanasi, and not an old image.

Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history.
The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen.
But analysts at Elliptic said the attacker had changed about $3.3 billion into digital assets that could not be frozen and was working to cash those out as traditional currency.
An “initial investigation” suggested hackers had been able to compromise an engineer’s laptop and withdraw funds from the platform, Binance said, adding on Friday morning that further investigation “has uncovered additional points of breach.” The company is working with law enforcement.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs linked the hack with a North Korean unit known as TraderTraitor, saying that the sums involved would make it “the largest crypto theft on record.” Last year, North Korean hackers stole crypto worth $1.5 billion in an attack on exchange Bybit.
Peter Ward, of the Sejong Institute in Seoul, said North Korea had considerable expertise and offered “near-total protection to its hackers.”
“Things may get a lot worse going forward,” he said.
Binance said on Friday that it had “already reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident,” with $5 billion of the funds “already held in the exact token assets that were impacted.”
The company said it was actively buying more tokens in order to cover the remaining amount. “This step can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity,” and settlement “also takes time,” it said.
The hack is a major blow to Binance, which was co-founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao and holds about $140 billion of digital assets. In 2023, the company pleaded guilty to US criminal charges related to breach of anti-money laundering laws and paid a $4.3 billion fine.

General Motors marketed its Smart Driver system as a way for parents to monitor teen drivers or for adults to track their driving behavior. But in 2024, it emerged that GM had been sharing that data with brokers. Those brokers then sold the data to insurance companies, and some drivers found that their insurance became more expensive as a result. To make matters worse, many of those drivers claimed they had no knowledge of ever agreeing to share such data for such purposes.
Last year, GM and its OnStar subsidiary entered into a settlement with the FTC, prohibiting them from sharing some kinds of driver data with third parties. The settlement was finalized this January. That agreement banned the two companies from sharing geolocation data or driver behavior data for five years. At the time, GM also discontinued Smart Driver across its entire range.
Now the automaker has reached terms with the District of Columbia and 35 states after their attorneys general joined together to sue GM as well.
GM told Reuters in a statement that “[s]afer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”
According to TechCrunch, the settlement with the states is notable in that it doesn’t take GM’s word that it’s complying with the privacy policy—a third party will be required to make that determination.
